first: चौ॰—जेहि समाज बैठे मुनि जाई। हृदय रूप अहमिति अधिकाई॥
en: The sage went and sat in the gathering, very proud in his heart of his looks. Shiva's two attendants sat there too, dressed as Brahmins, and no one knew what they were up to.

first: करहिँ कूटि नारदहि सुनाई। नीकि दोन्हि हरि सुन्दरताई॥
en: Making sure Narada heard, they joked, 'Hari has given him fine beauty! The princess will be charmed by his looks and choose him, thinking he is Hari himself.'

first: मुनिहि माह मन हाथ पराये। हँसहिँ सम्भु-गन अति सचु पाये॥
en: The sage's mind was caught by delusion and in another's hands, and Shiva's attendants laughed with great delight. Though the sage heard their odd words, he did not understand them, for his mind was clouded by confusion.

first: काहु न लखा सो चरित बिसेखा। सो सरूप नृप कन्या देखा॥
en: No one else saw this strange trick, but the princess saw his true form: a monkey's face and a frightful body. Seeing it, anger rose in her heart.

first: दो॰—सखी सङ्ग लेइ कुँवरि तब, चलि जनु राजमराल।
en: Then the princess set off with her friends, moving like a royal swan. With the victory garland in her lotus hands, she walked about looking at all the kings.

first: चौ॰—जेहि दिसि बैठे नारद फूली। सो दिसि तेहिन बिलाेकी भूली॥
en: She did not even by mistake look towards the side where Narada sat, swelling with pride. Again and again the sage rose up and grew restless, and Shiva's attendants smiled to see his state.

first: धरि नृप तनु तहँ गयउ कृपाला। कुँअरि हरषि मेलेउ जयमाला॥
en: The kind Lord went there in the form of a king, and the princess joyfully put the garland on him. Lakshmi's lord took the bride away, and all the kings were disappointed.

first: मुनि अति बिकल माह मति नाँठी। मनि गिरि गई छूटि जनु गाँठी॥
en: The sage was very upset; delusion had ruined his judgement. He felt as if a jewel had slipped out of a knot in his cloth and fallen. Then Shiva's attendants smiled and said, 'Go and look at your face in a mirror.'

first: अस कहि दोउ भागे भय भारी। बदन दीख मुनि बारि निहारी॥
en: Saying this, both ran off in great fear. The sage looked into water and saw his face. Seeing his form, his anger grew greatly, and he gave them a very harsh curse.

first: दो॰—हाेहु निसाचर जाइ तुम्ह, कपटी पापी दोउ।
en: 'You two cheats and sinners, go and be born as demons. You laughed at me; take the fruit of it. Laugh at a sage again if you dare!'

first: चौ॰—पुनि जल दीख रूप निज पावा। तदपि हृदय सन्तोष न आवा॥
en: When he looked into the water again, he saw his own form, but still his heart was not calm. His lips trembled with anger, and he set off at once to the lord of Lakshmi.

first: देइहउँ साप कि मरिहउँ जाई। जगत मेरि उपहास कराई॥
en: 'I will curse him, or I will die there; he has made me a laughing stock in the world.' Halfway along the road he met the enemy of the demons, with Lakshmi and that very princess.

first: बोले मधुर बचन सुर-साँई। मुनि कहँ चले बिकल की नाँई॥
en: The lord of the gods spoke sweetly: 'Sage, where are you going in such distress?' Hearing these words, great anger arose in him; under the power of maya, his mind lost all sense.

first: पर सम्पदा सकहु नहिँ देखी। तुम्हरे इरिषा कपट बिसेखी ॥
en: 'You cannot bear to see others' wealth; you are full of envy and deceit. When the ocean was churned, you drove Rudra mad, and through the gods you made him drink the poison.'

first: दो॰—असुर सुरा बिष सङ्करहिँ, आपु रमा मनि चारु।
en: 'You gave wine to the demons, poison to Shankar, and kept lovely Lakshmi and the jewel for yourself. You are crooked and selfish, always dealing in tricks.'

first: चौ॰—परम स्वतन्त्र न सिर पर कोई। भावइ मनहिँ करहु तुम्ह सोई॥
en: 'You are fully free, with no one over you, so you do whatever you please. You make good into bad and bad into good, and feel neither surprise nor joy at it.'

first: डहँकि डहँकि परचेउ सब काहू। अति असङ्क मन सदा उछाहू॥
en: 'You have cheated everyone so often that you have become bold in it; your mind is fearless and always eager for it. Good and bad deeds do not touch you, and no one has ever set you right till now.'

first: भले भवन अब बायन दीन्हा। पाबहुगे फल आपन कीन्हा॥
en: 'This time you have sent your gift to the right house; you will reap what you have sown. You cheated me by taking a certain body; my curse is that you will take that same body.'

first: कपि आकृति तुम्ह कीन्हि हमारी। करिहहिँ कीस सहाय तुम्हारी॥
en: 'You gave me the shape of a monkey, so monkeys will be your helpers. You have done me great harm, so you will suffer the pain of being parted from your wife.'

first: दो॰—साप सीस धरि हरषि हिय, प्रभु बहु बिनती कीन्ह।
en: The Lord gladly accepted the curse on his head and spoke many humble words to him. Then the ocean of mercy drew back the power of his maya.

first: चौ॰—जब हरि माया दूरि निवारी। नहिँ तहँ रमा न राजकुमारी॥
en: When Hari removed his maya, neither Lakshmi nor the princess was there. Then the sage, very frightened, held Hari's feet: 'Save me, you who remove the pain of those who bow to you!'

first: मृषा होउ मम साप कृपाला। मम इच्छा कह दीनदयाला॥
en: 'Kind Lord, let my curse be false.' The Lord kind to the humble said, 'It was my own wish.' The sage said, 'I spoke so many harsh words; how will my sins be wiped away?'

first: जपहु जाइ सङ्कर सत-नामा। होइहि हृदय तुरत बिस्रामा।
en: 'Go and repeat the hundred names of Shankar, and your heart will at once find peace. No one is as dear to me as Shiva; never, even by mistake, give up this faith.'

first: जेहि पर कृपा न करहिँ पुरारी। सो न पाव मुनि भगति हमारी।
en: 'Sage, one to whom the enemy of Tripura does not show grace cannot gain devotion to me. Keep this in your heart and go wander the earth; maya will not come near you now.'

first: दो॰—बहु बिधि मुनिहि प्रबोधि प्रभु, तब भये अन्तरधान।
en: After comforting the sage in many ways, the Lord vanished. Narada set off for the world of Brahma, singing the praises of Rama.

first: चौ॰—हर-गन मुनिहि जात पथ देखी। बिगत माह मन हरष बिसेखी॥
en: Shiva's attendants saw the sage going along the road, free of delusion and very happy at heart. Very frightened, they came to Narada, held his feet and spoke humbly.

first: हर-गन-हम न बिप्र मुनिराया। बड़ अपराध कीन्ह फल पाया॥
en: 'Great sage, we are not Brahmins but Hara's attendants. We did great wrong and have got its reward. Kind one, please soften the curse.' Narada, kind to the humble, spoke.

first: निसिचर जाइ होहु तुम्ह दोऊ। बैभव बिपुल तेज बल होऊ॥
en: 'Go, both of you, and be born as demons. You will have vast wealth, glory and strength. When you have conquered the world by the strength of your arms, Vishnu will take a human body.'

first: समर भरन हरि हाथ तुम्हारा। होइहहु मुकुत न पुनि संसारा॥
en: 'You will die in battle at Hari's hands and be set free, never to return to worldly life.' The two bowed their heads at the sage's feet and left, and in time they were born as demons.

first: दो॰—एक कलप एहि हेतु प्रभु, लीन्ह मनुज अवतार।
en: In one age, for this reason, the Lord came down as a man: Hari, who pleases the gods, gives joy to the good and removes the burden of the earth.

first: चौ॰—एहि बिधि जनम करम हरि केरे। सुन्दर सुखद बिचित्र घनेरे॥
en: In this way the births and deeds of Hari are many, lovely, joyful and wonderful. In age after age the Lord comes down and does lovely deeds of many kinds.

first: तब तब कथा मुनीसन्ह गाई। परम पुनीत प्रबन्ध बनाई॥
en: Each time, great sages have sung his story and made most holy poems of it. They have told many matchless tales, and the wise are not surprised on hearing them.

first: हरि-अनन्त हरि-कथा-अनन्ता। कहहिँ सुनहि बहु बिधि सब सन्ता॥
en: Hari is endless, and the story of Hari is endless; all saints tell it and hear it in many ways. The lovely deeds of Ramachandra cannot be fully sung even in millions of ages.

first: यह प्रसङ्ग मैँ कहा भवानी। हरि-माया मोहहिँ मुनि ज्ञानी॥
en: 'Bhavani, I have told this story to show that Hari's maya deludes even wise sages. The Lord is playful and does good to those who bow to him. He is easy to reach through service, and he removes every pain.'

first: सो॰—सुर नर मुनि कोउ नाहिँ, जेहि न माह माया प्रबल॥
en: There is no god, man or sage whom the strong maya does not delude. Thinking this over in your heart, worship the Lord of the great maya.

first: चौ॰—अपर हेतु सुनु सैलकुमारी। कहउँ बिचित्र कथा बिस्तारी॥
en: 'Daughter of the mountain, hear another reason. I will tell a wonderful story in full, of why Brahman, unborn, without qualities and without form, became the king of Kosala.'

first: जो प्रभु बिपिन फिरत तुम्ह देखा। बन्धु समेत धरे मुनि बेखा॥
en: 'The Lord you saw wandering in the forest with his brother, dressed as a hermit, Bhavani, whose deeds you saw and lost your wits while in Sati's body,'

first: अजहुँ न छाया मिटति तुम्हारी। तासु चरित सुनु भ्रम-रुज-हारी॥
en: 'even now the shadow of that has not left you. Listen to his deeds, which cure the disease of confusion. All the play he did in that coming to earth I will tell as far as my mind allows.'

first: भरद्वाज सुनि सङ्कर बानी। सकुचि सप्रेम उमा हरषानी।
en: Yajnavalkya said: 'Bharadvaja, hearing Shankar's words, Uma felt shy, loving and glad. Then the bull-bannered Shiva began to tell why that coming to earth took place.'

first: दो॰—साे मैँ तुम्ह सन कहउँ सब, सुनु मुनीस मन लाइ।
en: 'Great sage, I will tell you all of it; listen with an attentive mind. The story of Rama takes away the dirt of the dark age, brings blessings and is lovely.'

first: चौ॰—स्वायम्भुव-मनु अरु सतरूपा। जिन्ह तेँ मइ नर सृष्टि अनूपा॥
en: Svayambhuva Manu and Shatarupa, from whom the matchless human race came, were a husband and wife of fine conduct in dharma. The Vedas still sing of their example.

first: नृप उत्तानपाद सुत तासू। ध्रुव हरि-भगत भयउ सुत जासू॥
en: King Uttanapada was their son, whose son was Dhruva, the devotee of Hari. Manu's younger son was named Priyavrata, whom the Vedas and Puranas praise.

first: देवहूति पुनि तासु कुमारी। जो मुनि-कर्दम के प्रिय नारी॥
en: Devahuti was his daughter, the dear wife of the sage Kardama. She carried in her womb the first god, the kind Lord Kapila, merciful to the humble.

first: सांख्यसास्त्र जिन्ह प्रगट गखाना। तत्व बिचार निपुन भगवाना॥
en: The Lord Kapila, master of the study of truth, made the Sankhya teaching known. That Manu ruled for a long time and kept the Lord's commands in every way.

first: सो॰—होइ न बिषय बिराग, भवन बसत भा चौथ पन।
en: While still living at home, he reached the last stage of life, but his attachment to pleasures did not go. His heart felt great pain that his life had passed without devotion to Hari.

first: चौ॰—बरबस राज सुतहि नृप दीन्हा। नारि समेत गवन बन कीन्हा॥
en: The king gave the kingdom to his son even against his wish, and went to the forest with his wife. The best of holy places, famous Naimisha, is very pure and grants success to seekers.

first: बसहिँ तहाँ मुनि-सिद्ध-समाजा। तहँ हिय हरषि चले मनुराजा॥
en: Groups of sages and siddhas lived there, and King Manu went there with a glad heart. As the steady-minded pair walked along, they looked like knowledge and devotion in bodily form.

first: पहुँचे जाइ धेनुमति-तीरा। हरषि नहाने निरमल नीरा॥
en: They reached the bank of the Gomati and bathed happily in its clear water. Knowing him to be a royal sage devoted to dharma, siddhas and wise sages came to meet him.

first: जहँ जहँ तीरथ रहे सुहाये। मुनिन्ह सकल सादर करवाये॥
en: The sages respectfully took them to all the lovely holy places around. With thin bodies and wearing hermits' clothes, they listened daily to the Puranas among good people.

first: दो॰—द्वादस अच्छर मन्त्र पुनि, जपहिँ सहित अनुराग।
en: Then they lovingly repeated the twelve-syllable mantra, and the minds of husband and wife became fixed on the lotus feet of Vasudeva.

first: चौ॰—करहिँ अहार साक फल कन्दा। सुमिरहिँ ब्रह्म सच्चिदानन्दा॥
en: They lived on leaves, fruit and roots, and remembered Brahman, who is being, awareness and bliss. Then they began penance for Hari's sake, gave up roots and fruit, and lived on water alone.

first: उर अभिलाष निरन्तर होई। देखिय नयन परम प्रभु सेाई॥
en: A constant longing filled their hearts: to see with their own eyes that supreme Lord, without qualities, undivided, endless and without beginning, on whom the seekers of truth meditate;

first: नेति नेति जेहि बेद निरूपा। चिदानन्द निरुपाधि अनूपा॥
en: whom the Vedas describe as 'not this, not this'; who is pure awareness and bliss, free of all limits and beyond compare; from a part of whom many Shivas, Brahmas and Vishnus are born.

first: ऐसेउ प्रभु सेवक बस अहई। भगत हेतु लीला तनु गहई।
en: 'Even such a Lord is under the control of his servants and takes a body in play for his devotees. If what the Vedas say is true, then our wish will be fulfilled.'

first: दो॰—एहि बिधि बीते बरष षट,—सहस बारि आहार।
en: In this way six thousand years passed while they lived on water. Then for seven thousand years they lived on air alone.

first: चौ॰—बरष सहस-दस त्यागेउ सोऊ। ठाढ़े रहे एक पग दोऊ॥
en: For ten thousand years they gave up even that, and both stood on one foot. Seeing their boundless penance, Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva came to Manu many times.

first: माँगहु बर बहु भाँति लोभाये। परम धीर नहिँ चलहिँ चलाये॥
en: They tempted them in many ways, saying, 'Ask for a boon,' but the two were very steady and could not be moved. Their bodies were only bones, yet there was not the least pain in their minds.

first: प्रभु सर्बज्ञ दास निज जानी। गति अनन्य तापस नृप-रानी॥
en: The all-knowing Lord knew the ascetic king and queen as his own servants who looked to no one else. A voice from the sky, very deep and soaked in the nectar of grace, said, 'Ask, ask for a boon.'

first: मृतक–जिआवनि गिरा सुहाई। सवन–रन्ध्र होइ उर जब आई॥
en: When that lovely voice, which could bring the dead to life, entered their hearts through their ears, their bodies became strong, healthy and handsome, as if they had just come from home.

first: दो॰—स्त्रवन सुधा-सम बचन सुनि, पुलक प्रफुल्लित गात।
en: Hearing words like nectar to the ears, their bodies thrilled with joy. Manu bowed flat on the ground and spoke, his heart unable to hold its love.

first: चौ॰—सुनु सेवक सुरतरु-सुरधेनू। बिधि-हरि-हर-बन्दित पद-रेनू॥
en: 'Listen, you who are the wishing tree and wish-granting cow to your servants, the dust of whose feet Brahma, Hari and Hara worship. You are easy to reach by service and give every joy; you protect those who bow to you and rule all things moving and unmoving.'

first: जौँ अनाथ-हित हम पर नेहू। तौ प्रसन्न होइ यह बर देहू॥
en: 'Friend of the helpless, if you love us, then be pleased and grant us this boon: that form which lives in Shiva's mind, for which the sages strive,'

first: जो भुसुंडि-मन-मानस हंसा। सभुन अगुन जेहि निगम प्रसंसा॥
en: 'which is the swan in the Manasa lake of Bhushundi's mind, which the Vedas praise as with and without qualities: let us see that form to our eyes' content. Be kind, you who remove the pain of those who bow to you.'

first: दम्पति बचन परम प्रिय लागे। मृदुल बिनीत प्रेम-रस पागे॥
en: The words of husband and wife, gentle, humble and soaked in love, were very dear to the Lord. The Lord who loves his devotees, the ocean of mercy, who lives in all the world, appeared before them.

first: दो॰—नील-सरोरुह नील-मनि, नील-नीरधर-स्याम।
en: His body was dark like the blue lotus, the sapphire and the dark rain cloud. Seeing its beauty, millions upon millions of Kamas would feel ashamed.

first: चौ॰—सरद-मयङ्क-बदन छबि सीवाँ। चारु-कपाल चिबुक दर ग्रीवाँ॥
en: His face, like the autumn moon, was the height of beauty; his cheeks and chin were lovely and his neck like a conch. His lips were red, his teeth and nose handsome, and his smile put moonbeams to shame.

first: नव अम्बुज अम्बक-छबि नीकी। चितवनि ललित भावती जी की॥
en: His eyes had the fine beauty of fresh lotuses, and his graceful glance delighted the heart. His brows outshone Kama's bow, and a bright mark shone on his forehead.

first: कुंडल मकर मुकुट सिर भ्राजा। कुटिल केस जनु मधुप-समाजा॥
en: Fish-shaped earrings and a crown shone on his head, and his curly hair was like a swarm of bees. On his chest were the Shrivatsa mark, a lovely forest garland, a necklace with a pendant, and jewelled ornaments.

first: केहरि-कन्धर चारु जनेऊ। बाहु बिभूषन सुन्दर तेऊ॥
en: A fine sacred thread lay on his lion-like shoulders, and the ornaments on his arms were lovely too. His mighty arms were graceful like an elephant's trunk; a quiver was at his waist, and bow and arrow in his hands.

first: दो॰—तड़ित बिनिन्दक पीत-पट, उदर रेख बर तीनि॥
en: His yellow cloth outshone lightning; there were three fine lines on his belly. His navel was so lovely it seemed to steal the beauty of the whirlpools of the Yamuna.

first: चौ॰—पद-राजीव बरनि नहि जाही। मुनि मन मधुप बसहिँ जिन्ह माहीं॥
en: His lotus feet, in which the bee-like minds of sages dwell, cannot be described. At his left side, matching him, stood the first Power, a treasure of beauty and the root of the world,

first: जासु अंस उपजहिँ गुन खानी। अगनित लच्छि उमा ब्रह्मानी॥
en: from a part of whom countless Lakshmis, Umas and Sarasvatis, mines of virtue, are born, and by the play of whose brows the world comes to be. She is Sita, at Rama's left side.

first: छवि-समुद्र हरि रूप बिलोकी। एक टक रहे नयन पट रोकी॥
en: Seeing the form of Hari, an ocean of beauty, Manu and Shatarupa gazed without blinking, holding their eyelids still. They looked with reverence at that matchless form and could not have enough of it.

first: हरष-बिबस तनु दसा भुलानी। परे दंड इव गहि पद पानी॥
en: Overcome with joy they forgot their bodies and fell flat like sticks, holding his feet with their hands. The Lord, a mass of mercy, touched their heads with his lotus hands and at once raised them up.

first: दो॰—बोले कृपा-निधान पुनि, अति प्रसन्न माेहि जानि।
en: Then the ocean of mercy said, 'Knowing that I am very pleased, and thinking of me as a great giver, ask for whatever boon your heart desires.'

first: चौ॰—सुनि प्रभु बचन जोरि जुग पानी। धरि धीरज बोले मृदु बानी॥
en: Hearing the Lord's words, the king joined both hands, took courage and spoke gently: 'Lord, having seen your lotus feet, all our wishes are now fulfilled.'

first: एक लालसा बड़ि उर माहीँ। सुगम अगम कहि जाति सो नाहीँ॥
en: 'One great longing is in my heart. I cannot say whether it is easy or hard. For you, master, it is very easy to give, but to me, because of my smallness, it seems hard.'

first: जथा दरिद्र कल्पतरु पाई। बहु सम्पत्ति माँगत सकुचाई॥
en: 'Like a poor man who finds the wishing tree but is shy to ask for great wealth, because he does not know its power, so doubt arises in my heart.'

first: सो तुम्ह जानहु अन्तरजामी। पुरवहु मार मनोरथ स्वामी॥
en: 'You know it, for you dwell in every heart; fulfil my wish, Lord.' The Lord said, 'King, put aside your shyness and ask me; there is nothing I would not give you.'

first: दो॰—दानि-सिरोमनि कृपानिधि, नाथ कहउँ सतभाउ।
en: 'Ocean of mercy, crown of givers, Lord, I will tell you honestly; what can be hidden from the Lord? I want a son like you.'

first: चौ॰—देखि प्रीति सुनि बचन अमोले। एवमस्तु करुनानिधि बोले॥
en: Seeing his love and hearing his priceless words, the ocean of mercy said, 'So be it. Where can I go to find one like myself? King, I myself will come and be your son.'

first: सतरूपहि बिलोकि कर जोरे। देबि माँगु बर जो रुचि ताेरे॥
en: Seeing Shatarupa with joined hands, he said, 'Lady, ask for whatever boon you wish.' She said, 'Kind Lord, the boon my wise husband asked for is very dear to me.'

first: प्रभु परन्तु सुठि होति ढिठाई। जदपि भगत-हित तुम्हहिँ सुहाई॥
en: 'But, Lord, it is very bold of me, though you love to do good to your devotees. You are the father of Brahma and the other gods, lord of the world, Brahman, who knows every heart.'

first: अस समुझत मन संसय होई। कहा जो प्रभु प्रबान पुनि साेई॥
en: 'Thinking of this, doubt arises in my mind; yet what the Lord has said must surely come true. Lord, the joy and the state that your own true devotees gain,'

first: दो॰—साेइ-सुख साेइ-गति साेइ-भगति, सोइ निज चरन-सनेहु।
en: 'that same joy, that same state, that same devotion, that same love for your feet, that same wisdom and that same way of life, Lord, kindly grant us.'

first: चौ॰—सुनि मृदु गूढ़ रुचिर बच रचना। कृपासिन्धु बोले मृदु बचना॥
en: Hearing her gentle, deep and lovely words, the ocean of mercy spoke softly: 'Whatever wish is in your mind, I have granted it all; there is no doubt.'

first: मातु बिबेक अलौकिक तोरे। कबहुँ न मिटिहि अनुग्रह मोरे॥
en: 'Mother, by my grace your rare wisdom will never fade.' Then Manu bowed at his feet again and said, 'Lord, I have one more request.'

first: सुत-विषयक तव पद-रति होऊ। माेहि बड़ मूढ़ कहइ किन कोऊ॥
en: 'Let my love for your feet be as for a son, even if people call me a great fool. As a snake without its jewel or a fish without water, so let my life depend on you.'

first: अस बर माँगि चरन गहि रहेऊ। एवमस्तु करुनानिधि कहेऊ॥
en: After asking this boon he stayed holding his feet, and the ocean of mercy said, 'So be it. Now, as I command, go and live in the capital of the king of the gods.'

first: सो॰—तहँ करि भोग बिसाल, सात गये कछु काल पुनि।
en: 'Father, after enjoying great pleasures there for some time, you will become king of Ayodhya, and then I will be your son.'

first: चौ॰—इच्छामय नर-बेष सँवारे। होइहउँ प्रगट निकेत तुम्हारे॥
en: 'Taking a human form by my own will, I will appear in your house. Father, I will take a body together with my parts and do deeds that give joy to my devotees,'

first: जेहि सुनि सादर नर बड़भागी। भव तरिहहिँ ममता-मद त्यागी॥
en: 'hearing which with reverence, fortunate people will give up attachment and pride and cross the ocean of worldly life. My maya, the first Power who made the world, will also be born.'

first: पुरउब मैँ अभिलाष तुम्हारा। सत्य सत्य पन सत्य हमारा॥
en: 'I will fulfil your wish; my vow is true, true, true.' Saying this again and again, the Lord, the ocean of mercy, vanished.

first: दम्पपि उर धरि भगति कृपाला। तेहि आस्त्रमनि बसे कछु काला।
en: Holding devotion to the kind Lord in their hearts, the husband and wife lived in that hermitage for some time. When the time came, they left their bodies without pain and went to live in Amaravati.

first: दो॰—यह इतिहास पुनीत अति, उमहि कहा वृषकेतु।
en: Yajnavalkya said: 'The bull-bannered Shiva told this most holy story to Uma. Bharadvaja, now hear another reason for Rama's birth.'

first: चौ॰—सुनु मुनि कथा पुनीत पुरानी। जो गिरिजा प्रति सम्भु बखानी॥
en: 'Sage, hear this holy and ancient story, which Shambhu told to Girija. There was a land called Kaikaya, known to the world, where King Satyaketu lived.'

first: धरम-धुरन्धर नीति-निधीना। तेज प्रताप सील बलवाना॥
en: 'He upheld dharma and was a treasure of good rule, full of glory, power, good nature and strength. He had two brave sons, homes of every virtue and very steady in battle.'

first: राज-धनी जो जेठ सुत आही। नाम प्रताप-भानु अस ताही ॥
en: 'The elder son, heir to the throne, was named Pratapabhanu. The other son was named Arimardana, of matchless strength of arm and firm in battle.'

first: भाइहि माइहि परम समीती। सकल दोष छल वरजित प्रीती॥
en: 'The two brothers were close friends, and their love was free of all fault and deceit. The king gave the kingdom to his elder son and went to the forest himself to worship Hari.'

first: दो॰—जब प्रताप-रबि भयउ नप, फिरी दोहाई देस।
en: 'When Pratapabhanu became king, his rule was proclaimed through the land. He cared for his people strictly by the Vedas, and there was not a trace of sin anywhere.'

first: चौ॰—नृप-हित-कारक सचिव सयाना। नाम धरमरुचि सुक्र समाना॥
en: 'His minister, who worked for the king's good, was wise like Shukra, and was named Dharmaruchi. With a wise minister, a strong brave brother, and himself a mass of glory, steady in battle,'

first: सेन सङ्ग चतुरङ्ग अपारा। अमित सुभट सब समर जुझारा॥
en: 'he had with him a vast army of four kinds, with countless brave soldiers all eager for battle. Seeing his army, the king rejoiced, and the drums thundered loudly.'

first: बिजय हेतु कटकई बनाई। सुदिन साधि नृप चलेउ बजाई॥
en: 'He gathered an army for conquest, chose a good day, and set out with drums beating. Many battles were fought here and there, and he conquered all the kings by force.'

first: सप्त-दीप भुज-बल बस कीन्हे। लेइ लेइ दंड छाडि नृप दीन्हे॥
en: 'By the strength of his arms he brought the seven continents under his rule, took tribute from the kings and let them go. At that time Pratapabhanu was the one king of the whole earth.'

first: दो॰—स्वबस बिस्व करि बाहु बल, निज-पुर कीन्ह प्रबेस॥
en: 'Having brought the world under his rule by his own strength, he entered his city. The king enjoyed wealth, dharma, love and the other joys each in its proper time.'

first: चौ॰—भूप प्रताप-भानु बल पाई। कामधेनु भइ भूमि सुहाई॥
en: 'Under the strength of King Pratapabhanu, the earth became lovely like the wish-granting cow. His people were happy and free of all sorrow; men and women were handsome and good.'

first: सचिव धरमरुचि हरि-पद-प्रीती। नृप-हित-हेतु सिखव नित नीती॥
en: 'The minister Dharmaruchi loved Hari's feet and always taught the king good policy for his good. The king always served his guru, the gods, saints, ancestors and Brahmins.'

first: भूप-धरम जे बेद बखाने। सकल करइ सादर सुख माने॥
en: 'All the duties of a king described in the Vedas he did with respect and gladness. Every day he gave gifts of many kinds and listened to the scriptures, Vedas and Puranas.'

first: नाना बापी कूप तड़ागा। सुमन-बाटिका सुन्दर बागा॥
en: 'At all the holy places he built many fine step-wells, wells and lakes, flower gardens and lovely groves, and handsome homes for Brahmins and temples for the gods.'

first: दो॰—जहँ लगि कहे पुरान स्त्रुति, एक एक सब जाग।
en: 'Every sacrifice that the Puranas and Vedas describe, the king performed a thousand times over, with love.'

first: चौ॰—हृदय न कछु फल अनुसन्धाना। भूप बिबेकी परम सुजाना॥
en: 'He sought no reward in his heart; the king was very wise and thoughtful. Whatever good works he did in deed, mind and speech, the wise king offered to Vasudeva.'

first: चढ़ि बर बाजि बार एक राजा। भृगया कर सब साजि समाजा॥
en: 'Once the king mounted a fine horse and, with everything ready for hunting, went to the deep forest of the Vindhya hills, where he killed many fine deer.'

first: फिरत बिपिन नृप दीख बराहू। जनु वन दुरेउ ससिहि ग्रसि राहू॥
en: 'Wandering in the forest, the king saw a wild boar. It looked like Rahu hiding in the forest after seizing the moon; the moon was too big for its mouth, yet in anger it would not spit it out.'

first: कोल कराल दसन छबि गाई। तनु बिसाल पीवर अधिकाई॥
en: 'This is how the boar's fearful tusks are described. Its body was huge and very fat. Hearing the sound of the horse, it grunted, pricked up its ears and looked around in alarm.'

first: दो॰—नील-महीधर-सिखर सम, देखि बिसाल बराह।
en: 'Seeing the huge boar, like the peak of a dark blue mountain, the king spurred his horse and rushed on, shouting, "Now you cannot escape!"'

first: चौ॰—आवत देखि अधिकरव बाजी। चलेउ बराह मरुत-गति भाजी॥
en: 'Seeing the horse coming at great speed, the boar ran off as fast as the wind. The king at once fitted an arrow, and on seeing it the boar crouched flat on the ground.'

first: तकि तकि तीर महीस चलावा। करि छल सुअर सरीर बचावा॥
en: 'The king took aim again and again and shot, but the boar saved its body by tricks. Now showing itself, now hiding, the beast ran on, and the king, in anger, kept following it.'

first: गयउ दूरि धन-गहन बराहू। जहँ नाहिँन गज बाजि निबाहू॥
en: 'The boar went far into a thick forest where no elephant or horse could pass. The king was all alone and suffered great hardship in the forest, but still he did not leave the beast's trail.'

first: कोल बिलोकि भूप बड़ धीरा। भागि पैठ गिरि-गुहा-गँमीरा॥
en: 'Seeing that the king was very determined, the boar ran into a deep mountain cave. Seeing it could not be reached, the king was very sorry and turned back, but lost his way in the great forest.'

first: दो॰—खेद-खिन्न छुद्धित तृषित, राजा बाजि समेत।
en: 'Worn out with effort, hungry and thirsty, the king and his horse searched anxiously for a river or lake, and without water he became faint.'

first: चौ॰—फिरत बिपिन आस्रम एक देखा। तहँ बस नृपति कपट-मुनि बेखा॥
en: 'Wandering in the forest he saw a hermitage, where a king lived disguised as a sage. He was a king whose land Pratapabhanu had taken; he had left his army in battle and fled.'

first: समय प्रताप-भानु कर जानी। आपन अति असमय अनुमानी॥
en: 'Knowing that it was Pratapabhanu's time and that his own was very bad, he did not go home. His heart was full of shame, and being proud, he did not make peace with the king.'

first: रिस उर मारि रङ्क जिमि राजा। बिपिन बसइ तापस के साजा॥
en: 'Hiding his anger in his heart, that king lived in the forest like a poor man, in an ascetic's dress. When Pratapabhanu came near him, he recognised him.'

first: राउ तृषित नहिँ सो पहिचाना। देखि सुबेष महामुनि जाना॥
en: 'Being thirsty, the king did not recognise him; seeing his holy dress, he took him for a great sage. He got down from his horse and bowed, but, being very careful, he did not tell his name.'

first: दो॰—भूपति तृषित बिलोकि तेहि, सरवर दीन्ह दिखाय।
en: 'Seeing the king thirsty, he showed him a lake. The king happily bathed and drank, and so did his horse.'
